title: Current and Summit
premise: Ivo Amberdale, a desert ranger who has spent years outrunning a wrongful conviction, tracks a thief into the deep dunes and instead finds Halvard Brine, a prospector dying of heat and thirst. He trades her a map to the Sunken Summit—a buried river system that could water a hundred settlements—for her promise to bring his lost expedition's remains home. Following the map, Ivo uncovers not just water but proof that the magistrate who convicted her stole the land grants that created the drought in the first place. To get everyone home before the dry season seals the passes, she must lead a fractious crew of the dead man's kin and her old pursuers through hostile country, choosing between exposing the truth and keeping the water secret long enough to secure it. In the end, she delivers the expedition home, surrenders herself to face her conviction on her own terms, and lets the evidence—and the river—speak for her.
about_author: Ansel Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping arid basins before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who belong to landscapes more than to any law.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tracking a petty thief across the flats, Ivo reflects on why she never stops moving—stopping means questions, questions mean her name. She catches the thief but hesitates over the arrest, sensing he stole out of desperation. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She finds Halvard Brine dying at a dry well, map clutched to his chest. He offers it if she swears to bring his expedition's bodies home from the Sunken Summit. She takes the oath against her better judgment. Emotional beat: an unwanted inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deciphering the map, she realizes the Summit sits inside territory tied to her own old case—the land grants that ruined her family. The thief, Doss, begs to join her rather than hang. Emotional beat: the past closing like a trap.

chapters.title: Company of Strangers
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. The unlikely pair reaches the last settlement, where they recruit Sera Brine, Halvard's estranged daughter, who wants her father's body and nothing else. Tension flares: Sera distrusts rangers on principle. Emotional beat: grief wearing armor.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes Behind Them
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A rockslide seals their easiest route back; the dry season clock starts ticking loudly. Ivo reveals almost nothing of her plan, breeding resentment. Emotional beat: commitment without consent.

chapters.title: Salt Flats, Salt Wounds
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Crossing the flats, Doss confesses what he stole and why; Ivo gives him nothing back, but Sera notices how she watches the horizon like something might follow. Emotional beat: guarded trust forming.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ranger-corps trackers appear—led by Corvane, the officer who once arrested her. She hides the party and faces a choice: flee or mislead. She chooses misdirection, burning supplies to fake their deaths. Emotional beat: becoming someone new by erasing herself.

chapters.title: The First Marker
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They find the expedition's first camp: abandoned gear and a journal page proving Halvard found flowing water. Sera begins to understand what her father died chasing. Emotional beat: posthumous reconciliation beginning.

chapters.title: Night of the Sandstorm
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. A storm buries their route; they shelter in a cave where Ivo finally tells part of her story—not the crime, but the exile. Sera softens; Doss sees Ivo clearly for the first time. Emotional beat: vulnerability traded like currency.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Interlude: Corvane suspects Ivo lives and follows the same map fragment his superiors suppressed years ago. He knows the Summit's water was deliberately written off to protect land speculators. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Staircase
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They descend into the Summit canyon and find the second camp—and the first body, preserved in mineral crust. Sera breaks; Ivo holds the group together with sheer forward motion. Emotional beat: grief given a direction.

chapters.title: Water Under Stone
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They reach the buried river itself—an underground torrent beneath the dead summit. Wonder briefly unites them. Then they find the survey documents Halvard hid: proof the drought was manufactured by revoked grants. Emotional beat: awe weaponized.

chapters.title: The Weight of Proof
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Arguments erupt: take the water secret home quietly, or expose the magistrate? Ivo argues for silence until they're safe; Sera calls it cowardice dressed as caution. Emotional beat: justice versus survival splitting the group.

chapters.title: What Halvard Buried
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Reading Halvard's final journal pages, Ivo learns he knew who she was all along—he chose her because she'd been wronged by the same men. Her promise reframes as a summons. Emotional beat: being seen after years of hiding.

chapters.title: Corvane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane corners them at the canyon mouth, alone, having disobeyed orders to burn the evidence. He offers a deal: his testimony for theirs. Ivo must decide whether an enemy can become an ally. Emotional beat: enemies negotiating in good faith.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The merged party races the closing dry-season pass, carrying Halvard's body, the documents, and water samples. An injury forces a brutal pace decision. Emotional beat: shared purpose forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. One of Corvane's hidden men tries to destroy the documents; Doss stops him at real cost, wounded badly. Ivo realizes the conspiracy reaches higher than the magistrate. Emotional beat: sacrifice proving belonging.

chapters.title: Dry Season's Edge
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The pass will close within hours. Ivo splits the party—evidence goes ahead fast while she stays with the wounded and the body. She accepts she may not make it out. Emotional beat: leadership as self-erasure, one last time.

chapters.title: The Summit Speaks
chapters.summary: Climax, Ivo's POV. Ambushed at the pass by the magistrate's enforcers, Ivo stands her ground for the first time in the book, buying time as Sera escapes with the proof. She fights not to vanish but to be witnessed. Emotional beat: stillness chosen at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera delivers the documents to an assembly of settlement delegates; Corvane testifies. The grants are read aloud, the magistrate implicated, and the water claim filed in the expedition's name. Emotional beat: truth doing what force couldn't.

chapters.title: Homecoming, With Chains
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Rescued from the pass, Ivo walks into the settlement in custody, choosing to answer for her old charge openly. The crowd that once condemned her now carries Halvard's body beside her. Emotional beat: surrender as arrival.

chapters.title: Current and Summit
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating brief POVs. Cleared when Corvane's ledger surfaces, Ivo is offered the ranger post she once fled—and declines, taking instead the wardenship of the new river route. Sera names the spring for her father; Doss finds honest work. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.
